briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. As the specialized spokesperson for climate change, I will now begin today's climate briefing on October 8, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Biodiversity Crisis Threatening Survival
sections.content: Today's briefing begins with news of the severe crisis facing global biodiversity. Warnings that the population of 'chinstrap penguins' in the Antarctic region has sharply declined due to climate change, pushing them towards extinction, are being repeatedly reported both domestically and internationally. It is estimated that up to 680,000 penguin individuals have decreased [1, 5, 8, 10, 133, 138]. Such ecological disruptions, alongside large-scale changes like the 1.4-degree warming in the Amazon region [134], are leading to consequences such as a sharp drop in domestic red pepper yields [7] and human casualties from wild bear attacks in Mongolia [22], once again reminding us that climate change is a matter of survival.

sections.title: 🌍 International Community's Climate Action Discussions Towards COP31
sections.content: Ahead of COP31, the international community continues important discussions to address the climate crisis. Korea participated in the Pre-Conference of the Parties to the UNFCCC to discuss climate action measures, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' Ambassador for Climate Change held discussions on supporting climate-vulnerable nations at Pre-COP31 [2, 16]. The COP31 President emphasized that curbing global temperature rise is a matter of survival and requires urgency akin to defense spending, urging active action from the international community [130, 131]. Meanwhile, in the UK, viewers of a climate emergency briefing pointed out that their fellow citizens do not adequately perceive the scale of the climate crisis [124], indicating that raising public awareness of the climate crisis remains a crucial challenge.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Climate Change Response: Challenges and Efforts
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts to address climate change have been made, alongside the emergence of several challenges. During the 2026 National Assembly audit, it was pointed out that despite the severity of climate change, local governments' responses remain insufficient [6]. The issue of insufficient personnel and budget for renewable energy meteorological support at the Korea Meteorological Administration was also brought to light [63, 73, 81, 85, 87, 103, 108]. Furthermore, scientists who believe technology can solve climate change have shown a tendency to be passive in their personal actions [3], and an interesting study revealed that the use of the word 'environment' can actually hinder eco-friendly choices [4]. Nevertheless, adaptation efforts in the agricultural sector are continuing, with the Namwon City Council actively seeking to develop agricultural models for climate change response [9, 12] and the selection of cabbage varieties resilient to extreme weather [13].

sections.title: 🌱 Efforts Towards a Carbon-Neutral Society
sections.content: Amidst the climate crisis, positive domestic movements towards a carbon-neutral society continue. Daegu Metropolitan City set an innovative example by registering a project that utilizes landfill gas for heating and emission credits with the UNFCCC's 'Clean Development Mechanism' (CDM), a first in the nation [18]. Paju City engaged citizens directly to identify 26 carbon-neutral policies [26, 35, 46, 56, 60], and the Asan City Council launched a special committee for carbon neutrality to review policies and explore implementation strategies [25, 37, 38, 41, 45, 49, 50, 54]. Furthermore, Seongbuk-gu's Carbon Neutral Learning Center was designated as an excellent environmental education program [24, 62], and various local governments, including Incheon City and Gunwi County, are actively conducting citizen-participatory carbon-neutral campaigns and experiential events [20, 23, 27, 40, 42, 43, 48, 51, 52, 53, 57, 58, 59].

sections.title: 🌱 Renewable Energy and Green Technology Innovation and Current Challenges
sections.content: Efforts for renewable energy transition and green technology innovation are actively underway, but at the same time, numerous challenges remain to be addressed. Hyundai Engineering is participating in a national project to develop renewable energy-linked water electrolysis plant technology, strengthening its hydrogen production competitiveness [65, 66, 67, 70, 91, 92, 94, 97, 99, 101, 105, 106, 109, 113, 116, 117, 118, 119, 121], and renewable energy is gaining attention as a realistic alternative to the surging electricity demand in the AI era [64]. The government has set an ambitious target of achieving 30.2% renewable energy generation by 2030, stating its intention to pursue carbon neutrality and economic growth simultaneously through the K-GX strategy [33, 72, 69]. However, in an era aiming for 100GW of renewable energy, the Korea Meteorological Administration's specialized personnel for energy meteorology number only about 3.4, and the budget has been significantly reduced, making it urgent to strengthen power generation prediction capabilities [63, 73, 81, 103, 108]. Furthermore, despite the 100GW renewable energy target for four years from now, concerns have been raised about the lack of concrete plans for Energy Storage Systems (ESS) [100]. Internationally, the uncertainty in renewable energy policies is growing, with Germany dismantling its wind and solar departments and pushing for subsidy reductions [110].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlights the intersection of diverse response efforts from both the international community and domestic sectors amidst the severity of the climate crisis. Emphasizing once again that urgent action for survival, along with continuous technological innovation and policy support, is essential, I conclude today's climate briefing.
